t: You're at St Giles-without-Cripplegate, now set within the Barbican complex. It's one of the few medieval churches left in the City, having survived the Great Fire of 1666. It's dedicated to St Giles, patron saint of disabled and infirm people. John Milton, who wrote Paradise Lost, is buried here. So are the sea captain Martin Frobisher, who searched for the North-west Passage, and John Foxe, author of the Book of Martyrs. The mapmaker John Speed and the composer Giles Farnaby lie here too.
